title: Fit a spring tension rod between two cupboard walls so it holds itself up, level and at a marked height
instruction: Fit the spring tension rod between the two white cupboard walls, level, at the yellow band.
context: General maintenance and repair workers and property-maintenance staff fit spring tension rods for curtains, cupboard rails and shelf dividers where drilling is not allowed; one let go before both ends bear falls, and one set crooked holds but out of true. Unlike TK-8WZPBE (squeeze a cage fastener's legs; hooks retain it), nothing holds this rod up but its own spring and the grip of its end caps.
setup: 'In front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Cupboard walls (fixed, white painted board): two boards standing on the table, each 170 mm front to back (25.0 to 42.0 cm in front of the bases), 20 mm thick and 200 mm tall, their inner faces 150 mm left and 150 mm right of the midline (a 300 mm gap). Yellow band: a strip 20 mm wide, 30 mm tall and 2 mm proud on each wall's front edge (the face toward the robot), from 120 to 150 mm above the table. Spring tension rod (loose, 100 g in all): a blue-painted aluminium square tube 25 x 25 x 180 mm (1 mm wall) with a black rubber end cap 30 x 30 x 10 mm on its left end (60 g together), and a bare aluminium square inner tube 18 x 18 x 170 mm (1 mm wall) with an identical cap on its right end (40 g), which slides into the outer tube against a 70 N/m spring. Free length, cap face to cap face, 320 mm; it can be squeezed by up to 50 mm. It lies left to right, its middle 17.0 cm in front of the bases on the midline and its axis 42.5 mm above the table, on two risers, grey plastic blocks 40 mm front to back and 20 mm wide taped to the table: one 30 mm tall under the tube, 3 cm left of the midline, and one 33.5 mm tall under the inner tube, 6 cm right of the midline. Friction, static / sliding: rod and caps 1.0 / 0.8, walls 0.6 / 0.5. Spring damping 1 N s/m. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured after release: no credit while a gripper is within 5 mm of the rod. The rod holds itself up when it is let go and still (moving under 1 cm/s), both black caps press on the walls' inner faces (cap face within 0.3 mm of the wall, so the spring is pressing it there), each cap centre is on its wall's face (between the front and back edges, not above the top) and the rod is at least 3 mm clear of the table. Score 1.0: it holds itself up, each cap centre is at least 15 mm inside the front and back edges, neither cap's top is above the wall tops, both cap centres are 120 to 150 mm above the table (inside the yellow band), within 10 mm of the same height, and within 10 mm of each other front to back (the rod square across the gap). Score 0.5: it holds itself up but misses any of those placement limits: off the band, out of level, out of square or a cap over an edge. Score 0: anything else: the rod on the table, on the risers or across the wall tops, in front of or behind the walls, a cap short of its wall, still held, or sliding or falling. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 4 s; otherwise it scores the state at the last step.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Between trials: 1. Squeeze the rod and take it out from between the walls. 2. Let it spring back to its full 320 mm. 3. Check the two risers are taped 17 cm in front of the arm bases: the 30 mm one 3 cm left of the midline, the 33.5 mm one 6 cm right of it. 4. Lay the rod on them left to right, tube on the left, its middle on the midline. 5. Check the walls have not moved (inner faces 150 mm either side of the midline).
fidelity: Approximate. All parts are rigid boxes. The spring is a linear 70 N/m spring between the two tubes; fitted, the rod is squeezed 20 mm and presses each wall with about 1.4 N, enough to hold its own weight about 2.3 times over at the stated friction. Only the caps touch the walls. The cupboard is two fixed boards.
scores: Dream-1 run on the revised scorer: 0.0 (the rod stays on its risers). Scripted demo: 1.0 (the rod holds itself level in the band after both grippers withdraw).
